review: agree: सहज can go with अपावनि or with लहइ; the doubt is fairly recorded and the meaning gives the plain word order
agree: Rāma as Indra's dear younger brother (Upendra/Vāmana) is the usual reading; the alternative is fairly recorded

issue: सहज can go with अपावनि (impure by nature) or with लहइ (attains easily).
our reading: सहज अपावनि: a woman is impure by nature, yet by serving her husband she attains a blessed state.
alternatives: सहज = easily: even an impure woman easily attains a blessed state by serving her husband (milder, and fits 5.cau9's बिनु श्रम).

issue: शचीपति प्रियानुजम्: whom the epithet names (Rāma as Upendra/Vāmana, younger brother of Indra; or Lakṣmaṇa as Rāma's dear younger brother).
our reading: Rāma himself, the dear younger brother (Upendra) of Indra.
alternatives: Read with सानुजम्: Rāma, with Lakṣmaṇa, his dear younger brother; or leave the gloss (उपेन्द्र) out.

review: agree with the writer's reading (no favour to me; you kept your own vow); the doubt is fairly recorded
agree: 'free of desire' of the Lord is the plain reading; the alternatives are fairly recorded

issue: निहकाम: whether it describes the Lord dwelling in the heart (still, without desire) or the sage's own desireless request
our reading: the Lord dwells in the heart free of desire (निष्काम होकर)
alternatives: the sage asks this desiring nothing else (मैं निष्काम हूँ, बस यही दीजिये)
steady, unmoving like the moon (स्थिर)

issue: सो कछु देव न मोहि निहोरा: निहोरा as a favour/obligation done to me, or as my entreaty
our reading: this is no favour to me; you have kept your own vow
alternatives: I made no entreaty to you; you came of yourself, keeping your vow

issue: Which great sage's curse (उग्र साप मुनिबर कर) lies on the Daṇḍaka forest.
our reading: the great sage, unnamed, as the verse has it
alternatives: Śukrācārya, whose curse on King Daṇḍa laid the land waste (Gita Press English); Gautama (Gita Press Hindi)

issue: बगमेल: riding with reins together, in close array, or with reins let loose at full speed.
our reading: घोड़ोंकी बागें मिलाये / in close array
alternatives: बाग छोड़कर, बड़ी तेजीसे (Gita Press)

issue: ग्यान मान जहँ एकउ नाहीं: 'where there is not one (trace) of pride' or 'where there is not one of pride and the other faults'.
our reading: जिसमें मानका एक अंश भी नहीं / not a trace of pride
alternatives: मान आदि एक भी दोष नहीं (Gita Press); ज्ञान और मान — neither pride of knowledge nor honour

review: Agree: कंक is heron in Monier-Williams, a kite in Gita Press; keeping the name kaṅka is right.
Agree with 'over the ground' (धर = धरा); 'to catch me' is the alternative for the owner.

issue: कंक: which bird is meant (heron, or a carrion bird such as a kite).
our reading: Kept the name: कंक / the kaṅka, among carrion birds.
alternatives: heron (बगुला)
kite (चील)
crane (क्रौंच)

issue: धर: 'on the ground' (धरा, i.e. on foot) or 'to catch me' (धरना).
our reading: running after me over the ground
alternatives: running after me to catch me

review: Agree: our reading (Jaṭāyu's own wondrous deed, then remembering Rāma) is the plain one of करि; keep the doubt for the owner.
Agree it is a genuine doubt: असम सम can be 'peerless yet even' or 'uneven (partial to devotees) and even'; keep for the owner.
Agree: अनेक with मुनि is the natural reading; keep the doubt.
Agree: तुम per style.md §4 is right as written; the owner may choose आप for Jaṭāyu as an elder.

issue: सुमिरि राम करि अदभुत करनी: who did the wondrous deed, and what is remembered
our reading: Jaṭāyu, having done a wondrous deed (his fight), fell remembering Śrī Rāma
alternatives: He fell remembering Śrī Rāma's wondrous deeds (līlā)

our reading: peerless (none equal to him) yet even (impartial) to all
alternatives: uneven and even: partial to devotees yet impartial

issue: अनेक in करि ध्यान ग्यान बिराग जोग अनेक मुनि
alternatives: many practices (ध्यान, ज्ञान… and many more), sages attain him

issue: The Lord addresses Jaṭāyu, an elder (his father's friend, called तात) with honorific imperatives (राखहु, जाहु, कहहु); style.md has the Lord say तुम to others
alternatives: आप for Jaṭāyu as an elder

review: Agree with the writer: ताड़त here is the act of one Brahmin, not wording about a group, so the literal 'strikes' stands; the owner decides
Agree with the writer: करिबरगामिनी stands next to जनकसुता and reads as Sītā's epithet; as an address to the aged Śabarī it is unlikely
Agree with the writer: बार = देर (a long while) is the usual Awadhi sense with राखे … उर लाई

issue: करिबरगामिनी: an epithet of Sītā (जनकसुता) or a second address to Śabarī beside भामिनी
our reading: epithet of Sītā: news of Janaka's daughter, who walks with the grace of a noble elephant
alternatives: address to Śabarī: tell me, O lady of graceful gait

issue: बहुत बार in राखे बहुत बार उर लाई: बार = देर (for a long while) or बार = time (many times)
our reading: held him to his heart for a long while
alternatives: embraced him many times

issue: ताड़त: strikes/beats, or the milder rebukes/punishes (style §2 milder sense)
alternatives: rebukes, punishes (ताड़ना दे)

review: Agree: reading सुंदर अगम सुगम as qualifying the boons is the plain one; alternative fairly recorded.
Agree: सहरोसा is disputed (स+रोष 'emphatically' vs सहर्ष 'gladly'); 'ज़ोर देकर' is defensible; owner to decide.
Agree: 'Nārada said within himself' fits, since 45.cau2 then says Nārada spoke (बोले) again; narrator's comment is the alternative.

issue: सुंदर अगम सुगम: qualifies बर (boons) or Śrī Rāma himself
our reading: giver of fair boons, both hard and easy to attain
alternatives: Śrī Rāma is beautiful, unreachable (by effort) yet easily reached (by love), and a giver of boons

issue: सहरोसा: स+रोष 'with vehemence, emphatically' vs the word sheet's 'gladly'
alternatives: gladly, with joy (सहर्ष)
with mild reproach

issue: कहहु कवन प्रभु… (and 45.cau2 line 1): whose words — Nārada's inner thought or the narrator's exclamation; the verse names no speaker
alternatives: the narrator's (Śiva's) own comment
